KP 1. Limits at Infinity of Reciprocal Functions
1.?

Given that p(x)=2x4 and q(x)=1x2, what is limx→−∞p(x)q(x)?

M
Sat, Aug 8th @ 4:44 PM|Elapsed: 0:30Correct

First, we divide the two functions, as follows:

limx→−∞p(x)q(x)=limx→−∞(2x4)(1x2)=limx→−∞(2x2)

Now, we use the algebra of limits to pull out the constant factor of 2:

limx→−∞(2x2)=limx→∞(2⋅1x2)=2⋅limx→−∞(1x2)

Using the fact that

limx→−∞(1x2)=0,

We can evaluate our limit as follows:

2⋅limx→−∞(1x2)=2⋅0=0

limx→−∞p(x)q(x)=limx→−∞(−6x5)(3x2)=limx→−∞(−2x3)

Now, we use the algebra of limits to pull out the constant factor of −2:

limx→−∞(−2x3)=limx→−∞(−2⋅1x3)=−2⋅limx→−∞(1x3)

Now, using the fact that limx→−∞(1x3)=0,

we can evaluate our limit as follows:

−2⋅limx→−∞(1x3)=−2⋅0=0

limx→∞f(x)x3+5x−6=limx→∞f(x)⋅limx→∞1x3+5x−6

For any non-constant polynomial P(x), we have limx→±∞(1P(x))=0.

Therefore, since x3+5x−6 is a non-constant polynomial, we have limx→∞1x3+5x−6=0.

Sat, Aug 8th @ 4:52 PM|Elapsed: 0:08Correct
